text:
support-ops: Polaris (customer) escalated — sudden throughput drop and p99 spikes on hosted inference /v1/generate from 03:10–03:18 UTC. They saw 5s -> 18s p99 and ~40% throughput loss. Request id samples: r1=polaris-rcpt-823, r2=polaris-rcpt-829. Link to logs: https://logs.internal/polaris/1965432 :eyes:
maria: ack. adding @kevin @oliver. Any recent runtime or selector changes?
sre-bot: alert triggered: high-p99 (cfg=prod, model=gptq-7b, region=us-east-1). 03:09:58 -> 03:17:12. KV cache hitrate dropped from 86% -> 12% on these tenants.
kevin: I didn’t push selector changes today. There was an autoscaler bump around 02:50 that moved some pods to newer kernel builds. Checking rollout window.
oliver: I can take traces. Can someone run a lightweight replay of customer traffic (polaris scenario) against canary runtime? cmd: ./tools/replay --tenant polaris --qps 10 --duration 120 --profile --out /tmp/polaris.replay
maria: starting replay on staging cluster now, will forward perf logs.
lee: quick check — did they change prompt length distribution? longctxs can blow up p99 quickly.
support-ops: Polaris said they started a product E2E test at ~03:05 with longer instruction prompts (avg tokens/request up ~2.5x). Might be correlated.
kevin: nailed it — KV cache evictions spiked in logs, probably caused by sequence length jump + smaller batch packing hitting memory thresholds. Posting profiler snapshot: https://pprof.internal/polaris/1965432199
oliver: saw kernel selector fall back to slower GEMM path on a subset of machines (nvcc 12.2 -> compatibility issue). That explains p99 for certain instances.
maria: repro replay finished: aggregate p50=180ms, p95=1.2s, p99=6.9s on canary with current config. Baseline (yesterday) p99 ~700ms.
kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) route Polaris to region-us-west-2 pool where older kernels not rolled, 2) force kernel-optimized variant via routing policy for tenant, 3) enable temporary per-tenant batching cap to reduce mem churn. Thoughts?
support-ops: Polaris prefers quick fix — route traffic or roll back kernel. They asked for minimal change on their side.
lee: routing to us-west-2 is fastest. I'll open a routing override: route_set tenant=polaris -> pool=us-west-2-hot for 30m.
oliver: also gating model variant: set model_variant=gptq-7b-fast for polaris, which forces optimized kernels. patch: 
```
route override: tenant=polaris
  match: /v1/generate
  pool: us-west-2-hot
  model_variant: gptq-7b-fast
  ttl: 30m
```
kevin: after override, replay results: p99 dropped to 820ms, throughput recovered to 95% of baseline. KV cache hitrate back to ~80%. Good short-term.
maria: logging follow-up: we should capture taxonomy of requests that triggered evictions. I'll add extra labeling to request logs (longctx=true) for next 24h.
support-ops: Polaris confirms latency normalized after ~03:35. They want root cause analysis and ETA for full fix.
oliver: root cause hypothesis: kernel rollout + sudden longer prompts -> cache eviction -> fallback to slower GEMM path on some machines. Action items: kevin to validate kernel compatibility matrix and schedule rollback/patch; maria to add request labeling and retag telemetry; lee keep routing override until patch is deployed.
kevin: will run a binary compare across kernel builds and post delta by EOD. If rollback needed, I can coordinate with infra for a targeted rollback window tomorrow 02:00–03:00 UTC.
maria: I’ll assemble a short RCA draft and ETA to share with Polaris.
lee: override in place, monitoring for 30m. I’ll escalate to oncall if p99 > 2s again.
support-ops: thanks team — looping in Polaris CSM. Please post updates here and ping if you need help contacting customer. :thumbsup: 
kevin: quick note — command I ran: 
```
./infra/kernel_check --diff --from=nvcc-12.1 --to=nvcc-12.2 --machines us-east-1 > /tmp/kernel-diff.log
```
there are 3 changed kernels impacting fused attention paths.
oliver: will follow up with perf team for a proper patch. Closing this thread for now; keeping it monitored.
maria: RCA draft link: https://docs.internal/rca/polaris-1965432199 — will update.
lee: handled — marking owner=kevin for remediation.
